name: The traders in the temple
charge: Making the house of prayer a den of thieves
summary: At the passover Christ found in the temple those selling oxen and sheep and doves, and the changers of money sitting, made a scourge of small cords and drove them all out, poured out the money and overthrew the tables (John 2:13-16). The other account names what the place had become, a house of prayer turned into a den of thieves, in the words of Isaiah and Jeremiah (Matthew 21:12-13; Isaiah 56:7; Jeremiah 7:11). The trade was put out, the disciples remembered the writing about the zeal of God’s house, and the scribes and chief priests answered the correction by seeking how to destroy him (John 2:17; Mark 11:18).
offenseFull: The passover was at hand and he went up to Jerusalem, and found in the temple those that sold oxen and sheep and doves, and the changers of money sitting (John 2:13-14). This was during the feast, in the court of the house, and no man had business trading in there at the passover. What they had made of the place is named in the later account: the house of prayer turned into a den of thieves (Matthew 21:12-13; Mark 11:15-17), the words taken out of the prophets (Isaiah 56:7; Jeremiah 7:11). A den is where robbers go to divide what they have taken and to plan the next one. That is what the house of the Lord had been turned into.

Jeremiah had already described the leadership that let it get that way. They were waxen fat, they shone, they overpassed the deeds of the wicked, they judged not the cause of the fatherless, and they judged not the right of the needy, and still they prospered (Jeremiah 5:27-28). Men who live off the people will overlook the wickedness of whoever pays them. And the warning that stands next to the den of thieves is the place God had already destroyed for the wickedness of his people (Jeremiah 7:12): the house itself protects nobody who steals, murders, commits adultery and swears falsely and then comes and stands in it (Jeremiah 7:8-11). Zechariah said the day would come when there would be no more the trader in the house of the Lord of hosts (Zechariah 14:21).
judgmentFull: He made a scourge of small cords and drove them all out of the temple, with the sheep and the oxen, poured out the changers’ money and overthrew the tables, and told those that sold doves to take those things away and not make his Father’s house a house of merchandise (John 2:15-16). He drove grown men out of the temple with a whip. The Christ who did that was not the soft and mealy mouthed figure of the films; Mark adds that he would not allow a vessel to be carried through the temple, and that the scribes and chief priests heard it and sought how they might destroy him, because they feared him, since all the people were astonished at his doctrine (Mark 11:16-18). The men whose trade was overturned answered the correction with a plot.

His disciples remembered that it was written, that the zeal of God’s house had eaten him up (John 2:17; Psalms 69:9). When they demanded a sign for what he had done he spoke of the temple of his body raised up in three days, which went over their heads at the time and which false witnesses carried into his trial later on (John 2:18-22; Matthew 26:59-61). The judgment in this record is temporal and immediate: the trade driven out, the money on the floor, the tables turned over, the house cleared. The same trade goes on wherever money is extracted from our people in the name of the house, and the seat is defended instead of the flock, and the same correction stands written against it.

lawsResolved.text: True worship and service to God requires not formalism or excessive piety but to do justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with God.
Priests are to keep the charge of the sanctuary and tabernacle of the congregation and keep it supplied and in proper order.
Corruption is the way of those who are greedy of gain.
You shall not bring the hire of a harlot or the wages of a dog (male prostitute) into the house of the LORD your God for any pledge, vow or tithe.

text.text: And the Jews’ passover was at hand, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem,
And found in the temple those that sold oxen and sheep and doves, and the changers of money sitting:
And Jesus went into the temple of God, and cast out all them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the moneychangers, and the seats of them that sold doves,
And said unto them, It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.

And they come to Jerusalem: and Jesus went into the temple, and began to cast out them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the moneychangers, and the seats of them that sold doves;
And would not suffer that any man should carry any vessel through the temple.
And he taught, saying unto them, Is it not written, My house shall be called of all nations the house of prayer? but ye have made it a den of thieves.

Even them will I bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer: their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted upon mine altar; for mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people.
Is this house, which is called by my name, become a den of robbers in your eyes? Behold, even I have seen it, saith the Lord.
As a cage is full of birds, so are their houses full of deceit: therefore they are become great, and waxen rich.
They are waxen fat, they shine: yea, they overpass the deeds of the wicked: they judge not the cause, the cause of the fatherless, yet they prosper; and the right of the needy do they not judge.
But go ye now unto my place which was in Shiloh, where I set my name at the first, and see what I did to it for the wickedness of my people Israel.
Behold, ye trust in lying words, that cannot profit.
Will ye steal, murder, and commit adultery, and swear falsely, and burn incense unto Baal, and walk after other gods whom ye know not;
And come and stand before me in this house, which is called by my name, and say, We are delivered to do all these abominations?
Is this house, which is called by my name, become a den of robbers in your eyes? Behold, even I have seen it, saith the Lord.

Yea, every pot in Jerusalem and in Judah shall be holiness unto the Lord of hosts: and all they that sacrifice shall come and take of them, and seethe therein: and in that day there shall be no more the Canaanite in the house of the Lord of hosts.
And when he had made a scourge of small cords, he drove them all out of the temple, and the sheep, and the oxen; and poured out the changers’ money, and overthrew the tables;
And said unto them that sold doves, Take these things hence; make not my Father’s house an house of merchandise.
And would not suffer that any man should carry any vessel through the temple.
And he taught, saying unto them, Is it not written, My house shall be called of all nations the house of prayer? but ye have made it a den of thieves.
And the scribes and chief priests heard it, and sought how they might destroy him: for they feared him, because all the people was astonished at his doctrine.
And his disciples remembered that it was written, The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up.
For the zeal of thine house hath eaten me up; and the reproaches of them that reproached thee are fallen upon me.
Then answered the Jews and said unto him, What sign shewest thou unto us, seeing that thou doest these things?
Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.
Then said the Jews, Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou rear it up in three days?
But he spake of the temple of his body.
When therefore he was risen from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this unto them; and they believed the scripture, and the word which Jesus had said.
Now the chief priests, and elders, and all the council, sought false witness against Jesus, to put him to death;
But found none: yea, though many false witnesses came, yet found they none. At the last came two false witnesses,
And said, This fellow said, I am able to destroy the temple of God, and to build it in three days.
